metadata.title: Cardano Node And JorManager Tracing Migration Tasks
metadata.description: Migrate new JorManager-managed nodes to cardano-node 11.0.1 dispatcher tracing and make direct JorManager <-> node Hermod-compatible protocols the only integration boundary for logs and node-state data.
metadata.importantNote: Direct JorManager <-> node Hermod-compatible protocols are the only accepted integration boundary in this plan. Remove all EKG and Prometheus HTTP polling and all generated EKG or Prometheus HTTP node config.

phases.name: Schema And Provisioning Foundation
phases.description: Add the persistent tracing metadata needed to provision core nodes and carry direct protocol configuration through node creation.

tasks.title: Add tracing port persistence for nodes
tasks.description: Add database and entity support for a per-node tracing port so core nodes can expose a dedicated tracing listener without relying on EKG or Prometheus HTTP ports.
implementationNotes: Add nodes.tracing_port through a Liquibase migration.
Extend the Node entity and any repository projections or DTO plumbing that rely on the nodes table shape.
Keep tracing_port nullable for relay and pool nodes in phase 1.
testCases: Application starts cleanly with the new migration.
Existing node reads tolerate null tracing_port values.
Core-node serialization exposes tracingPort if present.
acceptance: Database schema includes nodes.tracing_port.
Backend model can persist and read tracingPort values.
No tracing-specific UI controls are added.
tasks.completionNotes: Added nullable Node.tracingPort persistence and Liquibase changeset 039 without widening into controller, request-model, UI, or live Liquibase execution. Manual schema application is deferred to later end-to-end validation.

tasks.title: Allocate and save core tracing ports
tasks.description: Teach node creation to allocate a tracing port for core nodes, persist it, and leave relay and pool nodes unassigned in the first version.
implementationNotes: Use a tracing-port allocation strategy that does not depend on EKG or Prometheus HTTP ports.
Persist tracingPort only for core nodes.
Avoid adding a user-facing tracing port field in the first version unless backend flow proves it is required.
testCases: Core node creation allocates a tracing port.
Port collisions scan upward correctly.
Relay and pool creation leave tracingPort null.
acceptance: Core nodes receive a dedicated tracing port during creation.
Tracing port persistence is deterministic and host-local.
No tracing port is requested from the user in phase 1.
tasks.completionNotes: Added a minimal NodeController tracing-port allocation helper for core nodes that scans upward with the existing host-local port probe, persists null for relay/pool nodes, and adds focused helper tests. Focused Gradle verification was attempted but backend Kotlin compilation remains blocked by unrelated pre-existing NodeController extension import/call-site failures in the workspace.

phases.name: Node Config And Startup Migration
phases.description: Replace legacy file-tracing generation with dispatcher-era tracing config, remove generated EKG and Prometheus HTTP config, pin the listener mechanism for automated implementation, and wire core-node trace forwarding into startup generation.

tasks.title: Build dispatcher tracing config logic from Markus baseline
tasks.description: Replace the legacy regex-driven config mutation path with app-side config generation logic that starts from the Markus tracing baseline and applies only the required 11.0.1 dispatcher-era mutations, without generating EKG or Prometheus HTTP config.
implementationNotes: Preserve Markus as the tracing baseline.
Set UseTraceDispatcher true for all generated node configs.
Preserve Stdout MachineFormat.
Add Forwarder only for core nodes.
Remove EKGBackend, PrometheusSimple, hasEkg, hasEKG, and any HTTP metrics bindings from generated configs.
Retain only the compatibility-era top-level non-HTTP tracing keys still needed by cardano-node 11.0.1.
testCases: Core config includes dispatcher tracing and forwarder backend.
Relay and pool config include dispatcher tracing without forwarder backend.
Generated config does not include EKG or Prometheus HTTP configuration.
Generated config does not emit file-log scribes or rotation config.
Generated config carries required compatibility-era top-level keys.
acceptance: Config generation no longer depends on legacy file-log assumptions.
Config generation no longer emits EKG or Prometheus HTTP config.
Generated tracing config is based on Markus plus minimal JorManager-owned mutations.
Core and non-core node tracing shapes differ only where the PRD allows.
tasks.notes: A small structured config builder is preferred over more regex patching of legacy config blobs.
tasks.completionNotes: Replaced the live NodeController tracing-config regex path with a structured JSON-tree helper that seeds TraceOptions from an explicit Markus-derived baseline, applies the pinned dispatcher-era relay/core mutations, removes legacy tracing and HTTP metrics keys from generated output, and adds focused NodeControllerTest coverage for Markus-based relay/core config shape. Rollout remains gated behind later listener, consumer-migration, and template-alignment tasks.

tasks.title: Pin the automated tracing listener mechanism
tasks.description: Verify and codify the exact cardano-node 11.0.1 tracing listener/startup mechanism so the agentic implementation can rely on fixtures and tests instead of manual runtime discovery.
implementationNotes: Turn the accepted listener shape into a reproducible fixture or documented config/startup artifact under the tracing plan research area or test resources.
Avoid leaving listener verification as an implicit manual coding-time activity.
Capture enough detail that prompt.md can implement startup wiring without operator intervention.
testCases: A fixture or focused test pins the accepted listener/startup shape for cardano-node 11.0.1.
The verified listener mechanism is expressible through JorManager-generated artifacts.
The implementation path no longer depends on interactive runtime experimentation.
acceptance: The tracing listener mechanism is explicitly verified and documented in code-adjacent artifacts.
Subsequent startup-generation work can be implemented in an automated fashion.
No user interaction is required to choose between config-only and CLI-only wiring during implementation.
tasks.completionNotes: Pinned the verified `cardano-node 11.0.1` listener mechanism to a reusable `NodeController.renderTracingListenerArgument()` helper and focused `NodeControllerTest` coverage for the exact core-only `--tracer-socket-network-accept 0.0.0.0:<tracingPort>` fragment. Also recorded that task-102 must reconcile startup-artifact generation ordering and persisted-input flow before wiring the helper into systemd/manual startup commands.

tasks.title: Wire core tracing listener into startup generation
tasks.description: Update systemd or manual startup generation so newly created core nodes actually listen for the trace-forward client on the saved tracing port.
implementationNotes: Use the verified cardano-node 11.0.1 listener mechanism rather than guessing between config-only and CLI-only wiring.
Bind listeners as required by the PRD and preserve existing service-generation conventions where possible.
Keep forwarding limited to core nodes.
testCases: Generated startup wiring includes trace-forward listener settings for core nodes.
Relay and pool startup wiring does not expose a trace-forward listener.
Existing non-tracing startup settings remain intact.
acceptance: New core-node startup artifacts contain the verified tracing listener configuration for cardano-node 11.0.1.
Generated startup artifacts remain consistent with JorManager's existing deployment style.
No runtime dependency on cardano-tracer is introduced.
tasks.completionNotes: Updated NodeController startup generation so direct core creation allocates tracingPort before writing systemd/manual artifacts, centralized listener wiring through renderTracingListenerArgument-backed render helpers, and preserved the existing pool parent-core bulk-credentials systemd shape while adding the core-only listener from persisted coreNode.tracingPort. Focused NodeControllerTest coverage now pins direct core, relay, and pool-triggered parent-core rewrite listener behavior, including the null-port no-listener case.

tasks.title: Remove EKG and Prometheus HTTP request plumbing
tasks.description: Remove EKG and Prometheus HTTP port fields from backend request models and new-node UI plumbing so the new direct-protocol design is reflected before monitor migration completes.
implementationNotes: Remove EKG and Prometheus HTTP port fields from CreateNodeRequest and AddNodeWizard for new-node creation.
Keep frontend changes internal-only and do not add tracing controls.
Do this early so downstream implementation and tests no longer carry obsolete request assumptions.
testCases: New-node request models no longer require EKG or Prometheus HTTP ports.
New-node UI plumbing no longer exposes EKG or Prometheus HTTP port inputs.
No tracing-specific user interaction is introduced.
acceptance: No new-node UI or API surface remains for EKG or Prometheus HTTP ports.
Request and UI plumbing align with the direct-protocol design before monitor migration completes.
No user interaction is required for tracing-related new-node inputs.
tasks.completionNotes: Removed request and wizard exposure of EKG/Prometheus ports, replaced request-fed controller usage with an internal metrics-port allocation seam that preserves persisted `Node.ekgPort`/`Node.promPort` and core tracing-port sequencing, and verified the change with focused NodeController tests plus a required Vue production build. Runtime HTTP metrics behavior for newly created nodes remains intentionally gated behind later monitor migration tasks.

phases.name: Direct Protocol Consumer Subsystem
phases.description: Introduce the direct Hermod-compatible client stack that can connect to core nodes, using automated fixtures first, then decode forwarded trace objects and normalize the block data JorManager needs in the first implementation wave.

tasks.title: Add core tracing connection lifecycle management
tasks.description: Create the first pass of a dedicated Hermod-compatible subsystem that manages the required long-lived node protocol session(s) per core node and handles reconnects without depending on SSH, cardano-tracer, or a Hermod sidecar.
implementationNotes: Keep the tracing subsystem separate from the existing node-to-client mini-protocol code even if lifecycle patterns are reused.
Manage the required long-lived Hermod-compatible session or sessions per forwarded core node without overcommitting to a single-session topology.
Make reconnect and shutdown behavior explicit and testable.
testCases: Subsystem opens the required tracing session or sessions per eligible core node.
Connection loss triggers reconnect behavior.
Deleting or disabling a node tears down its tracing session cleanly.
acceptance: JorManager has a dedicated tracing connection manager or equivalent service.
The subsystem is independent from SSH log scraping.
The subsystem can be extended to more Hermod-compatible event or state families later.
tasks.completionNotes: Added a new production tracing lifecycle package with a dedicated `TracingConnectionManager`, a minimal direct TCP trace-forward session client, and a single raw-message sink seam for later decoder work. Focused lifecycle tests now cover seeded startup, reconnect on disconnect, idempotent duplicate node refreshes, ineligibility teardown, idle-session stability, and both Spring stop paths; the final Gradle verification passed, though current repo wiring also runs Vue unit tests and frontend build during the backend target.

tasks.title: Add automated protocol fixtures for tracing implementation
tasks.description: Create synthetic protocol fixtures or a lightweight simulated server so Hermod-compatible lifecycle, decode, and reconnect behavior can be implemented and tested without depending on live node experimentation.
implementationNotes: Prefer committed fixtures or a lightweight fake server under test resources over manual integration-only validation.
Make the artifacts reusable by both the block-event and node-state workstreams.
Optimize for prompt.md-driven implementation and regression coverage.
testCases: Tracing client tests can run against synthetic protocol fixtures or a simulated server.
Reconnect behavior is testable without live remote nodes.
Decoder behavior can be exercised with reproducible payload fixtures.
acceptance: The implementation path no longer depends primarily on live-node manual testing.
Automated fixtures exist for the direct Hermod-compatible protocol work.
The same fixtures can be reused in later node-state migration work.
tasks.completionNotes: Added a test-only tracing fixture package with independent CBOR byte anchors for the minimum request/reply/done session contract, a scripted fake server for repeated-session reconnect scenarios, and forwarded adopted-block wrapper fixtures that preserve the PRD-pinned `toNamespace`/`toMachine` boundary without guessing node-state payload families. Focused Gradle verification passed, though the repo's current build wiring also ran Vue tests and production build during the backend test target.

tasks.title: Decode forwarded adopted-block trace objects
tasks.description: Implement the decoder that matches Forge.AdoptedBlock forwarded TraceObjects and extracts the cardano-node 11.0.1 TraceAdoptedBlock machine payload into a normalized internal block event.
implementationNotes: Match on forwarded namespace Forge.AdoptedBlock.
Parse toMachine JSON and confirm kind TraceAdoptedBlock.
Phase 1 should depend only on slot and blockHash and tolerate optional blockSize or txIds fields.
testCases: Valid Forge.AdoptedBlock payloads decode into normalized block events.
Unexpected namespaces are ignored.
Malformed toMachine JSON does not crash the subsystem.
Payloads missing required slot or blockHash are rejected safely.
acceptance: Forwarded adopted-block events decode without relying on the old scraped log-line model.
Namespace and kind checks are both enforced.
Decoder output is suitable for reuse by BlockMonitor migration work.
tasks.completionNotes: Added a small tracing-package decoder that traverses non-empty `TraceObjectsReply` payloads, matches only forwarded `Forge.AdoptedBlock` plus machine `kind: "TraceAdoptedBlock"`, and normalizes machine-owned `slot`/`blockHash` with forwarded `toTimestamp`/`toHostname` into a reusable internal event. Focused decoder and fixture tests passed, including malformed JSON, wrong kind, non-numeric slot, wrapper-only blockHash rejection, and scripted non-empty reply traversal; current Gradle wiring also ran Vue tests/build during verification.

tasks.title: Bridge tracing events into block persistence flow
tasks.description: Add the service layer that takes normalized adopted-block events from the tracing client and hands them into the existing block repository flow with minimal disruption to downstream validation semantics.
implementationNotes: Preserve trace-driven discovery followed by chain-driven forged or missed or orphaned classification.
Keep websocket updates and repository writes behaviorally aligned with the existing monitor.
Avoid coupling the tracing subsystem directly to SSH or host shell utilities.
testCases: A normalized adopted-block event results in a saved candidate block.
Existing validation loop still resolves forged or missed or orphaned status later.
Duplicate adopted-block events do not create duplicate persisted blocks.
acceptance: Tracing events can drive candidate block persistence end to end.
Current downstream validation semantics remain intact.
No new historical replay behavior is introduced.
tasks.completionNotes: Added a real production `TraceForwardMessageSink` path that decodes forwarded adopted-block replies and persists candidate blocks through a shared tracing persistence service, while preserving managed-host persistence, websocket publication, and `BlockUtils`-based epoch/slot-in-epoch calculation. Follow-up review exposed a duplicate-race risk while legacy SSH/file discovery still coexists, so the final approved implementation moved duplicate suppression behind a shared persistence mutex and added focused interleaving coverage; the focused Gradle verification passed, and this repo also ran Vue tests/build during that target.

tasks.title: Pin the node-state protocol family and mapping
tasks.description: Pin the exact direct Hermod-compatible node-state protocol family used in this version and verify how its payloads normalize into the current NodeStats contract.
implementationNotes: Make an explicit design decision for this version between forwarded trace objects, data-point style exchanges, or another Hermod-compatible node-state family.
Create the equivalent of the block-event decoder task for node-state data before refactoring NodeMonitor.
Pin the mapping for peers, incomingPeers, blockHeight, remainingKESPeriods, epoch, slot, slotInEpoch, and txsProcessed.
Use automated fixtures instead of relying on manual node inspection.
testCases: Node-state payload fixtures map cleanly into the current NodeStats shape.
Missing or malformed node-state fields fail safely.
The mapping can be reused by the later NodeMonitor refactor.
acceptance: The node-state protocol family is explicitly pinned for the first migration version.
A concrete node-state mapping exists before NodeMonitor is refactored.
Node-state migration is no longer under-specified compared with block-event migration.
The mapping is covered by automated tests.
tasks.completionNotes: Pinned the first node-state migration version to the direct DataPoint mini-protocol, codified the exact eight `cardano.node.metrics.*` keys and NodeStats mapping in a small sibling tracing decoder/client surface, and added independent literal CBOR request/reply anchors plus negative and chunked-byte fixtures so the protocol contract is testable without live-node discovery. Focused Gradle verification passed, and the repo's current test graph also ran Vue tests and frontend production build during that command.

phases.name: Monitor Migration
phases.description: Replace the old discovery and polling paths with direct Hermod-compatible consumers once the protocol foundation is automated and testable.

tasks.title: Remove SSH and file scraping from BlockMonitor
tasks.description: Delete the legacy historical scrape and live tail code paths from BlockMonitor so block discovery comes only from the new tracing subsystem.
implementationNotes: Remove dependency on logs/node.json, logs/node-*.json, tail, grep, and SSH-based discovery for block monitoring.
Keep the validation loop only where it still belongs.
Remove obsolete parsing helpers once the tracing handoff covers discovery fully.
testCases: BlockMonitor no longer shells out to tail or grep.
BlockMonitor no longer opens SSH sessions for block discovery.
Block validation still runs on discovered candidate blocks.
acceptance: No runtime dependency remains on node log files for block discovery.
BlockMonitor is simplified to tracing-driven discovery plus validation.
Legacy discovery-only code is removed rather than left dormant.
tasks.completionNotes: Removed the legacy SSH and local-shell block discovery path from BlockMonitor entirely, preserved the existing cold-start nodesChannel seed that adjacent monitors still depend on, retained only candidate-block validation semantics, and added focused BlockMonitor tests for startup seeding plus forged/missed/orphaned outcomes. Focused Gradle verification passed, and the repo's configured test graph also ran Vue tests and frontend production build during that target.

tasks.title: Replace NodeMonitor HTTP metrics polling with direct node protocol consumption
tasks.description: Refactor NodeMonitor so the current NodeStats data comes from direct Hermod-compatible node protocol consumption rather than EKG or Prometheus HTTP polling or SSH port-forwarding.
implementationNotes: Preserve the NodeStats contract where practical while changing the underlying source.
Remove dependency on EkgService and on node HTTP endpoint polling.
Remove SSH port-forwarding used only to reach node HTTP metrics surfaces.
Use the same direct protocol boundary as the tracing subsystem rather than introducing a sidecar.
testCases: NodeMonitor no longer polls EKG HTTP endpoints.
NodeMonitor no longer polls Prometheus HTTP endpoints.
NodeMonitor no longer uses SSH port-forwarding for HTTP metrics collection.
Decoded node-state data still produces the current NodeStats fields.
acceptance: NodeMonitor is no longer coupled to HTTP EKG or Prometheus endpoints.
Dashboard node stats are fed by direct node protocol consumption.
The direct protocol subsystem covers both block flow and node-state flow.
tasks.completionNotes: Replaced NodeMonitor's Retrofit EKG and SSH port-forward polling path with direct short-lived DataPoint sessions against core-node tracing listeners, added startup self-seeding plus core-only eligibility handling inside NodeMonitor, and preserved the existing NodeStats contract, websocket payload shape, and default-node cache semantics within the approved core-only boundary. Follow-up review corrected the pinned DataPoint mini-protocol so JorManager sends client-side MsgDone after the first reply, and focused Gradle verification passed with new NodeMonitor coverage plus the existing node-state decoder and tracing lifecycle tests; the repo task graph also ran Vue tests and frontend production build during that target.

tasks.title: Retire HTTP-only metrics plumbing
tasks.description: Retire EkgService and any remaining HTTP-only metrics plumbing once BlockMonitor and NodeMonitor have both moved to the direct Hermod-compatible boundary.
implementationNotes: Retire EkgService or any equivalent HTTP-only client once no call sites remain.
Do not remove HTTP-only plumbing until direct replacements are already in place.
Keep this cleanup separate from docs synchronization.
testCases: No production call site remains for EkgService or equivalent HTTP-only metrics clients.
NodeMonitor behavior remains intact after HTTP-only client retirement.
acceptance: HTTP-only metrics plumbing is retired only after direct replacements are live.
The codebase no longer carries an active EKG or Prometheus HTTP metrics path.
tasks.completionNotes: Deleted the orphaned `EkgService` interface and the unused `model/ekg` plus `model/ekg2` HTTP metrics DTO trees after confirming task-301 had fully moved `NodeMonitor` to the direct DataPoint path. Focused backend verification passed with NodeMonitor and tracing tests, and the repo's Gradle wiring also ran Vue unit tests and frontend production build during that target; persisted `Node.ekgPort` and `Node.promPort` intentionally remain for the later controller/schema cleanup that still depends on them.

phases.name: Release Alignment And Docs
phases.description: Apply environment-facing template updates and synchronize planning artifacts after the automated code path is already implemented.

tasks.title: Update deployed node template configs
tasks.description: Update the deployed node template configs under /home/westbam/bcsh/jormanager so new node creation for guild, mainnet, preprod, and preview inherits the dispatcher-era tracing setup without EKG or Prometheus HTTP config.
implementationNotes: Update only guild-config.json, mainnet-config.json, preprod-config.json, and preview-config.json.
Keep db-sync config files explicitly out of scope.
Apply the same dispatcher-era tracing rules used by the JorManager config-generation design after the app-side implementation is already proven.
Remove legacy file-log assumptions and all EKG or Prometheus HTTP config from the deployed templates.
testCases: All four deployed node template configs use dispatcher tracing.
All four deployed node template configs preserve machine-formatted stdout logging.
No updated template carries legacy file-log scribes, rotation assumptions, or EKG or Prometheus HTTP config.
No *-db-sync-config.json file is modified.
acceptance: guild-config.json, mainnet-config.json, preprod-config.json, and preview-config.json are updated for the tracing migration.
The deployed template configs align with the PRD's dispatcher-era direct-protocol model.
db-sync config templates remain untouched.

tasks.title: Sync plan docs and prompt artifacts
tasks.description: Update PRD, tasks, research notes, and prompt-driven implementation guidance after the direct-protocol implementation is stable.
implementationNotes: Keep doc synchronization separate from core implementation tasks.
Ensure prompt.md guidance reflects the final automated implementation path.
Only do this after the implementation truth is known.
testCases: PRD and tasks reflect the implemented sequencing and design.
Research notes still point to the correct implementation references.
Prompt-oriented guidance matches the final architecture.
acceptance: Plan artifacts are synchronized with the implemented result.
Prompt-driven implementation guidance no longer depends on stale assumptions.
Documentation work does not block core implementation.

riskAreas: Verifying the exact cardano-node 11.0.1 tracing listener startup mechanism.
Implementing the Hermod-compatible wire client without overfitting to cardano-tracer or Hermod sidecar internals.
Keeping the deployed node template configs in /home/westbam/bcsh/jormanager aligned with the app-side tracing model.
Replacing BlockMonitor discovery without regressing forged or missed or orphaned classification semantics.
Preserving NodeMonitor dashboard semantics while removing EKG and Prometheus HTTP polling.
Keeping the implementation path fully automatable through fixtures instead of manual runtime experimentation.
Migrating config generation away from legacy regex mutation safely.
summary.testingNotes: Prioritize focused backend coverage for config generation, tracing port allocation, listener/startup fixtures, Hermod-compatible trace object decoding, tracing connection lifecycle, reusable protocol fixtures, NodeMonitor node-state decoding, and end-to-end candidate block persistence. Frontend checks should stay limited to removing obsolete EKG and Prometheus HTTP inputs from new-node creation.
summary.rollbackPlan: Disable or revert the tracing migration as a unit by restoring the previous node config generation and BlockMonitor discovery path from git if implementation verification fails before release. Newly created nodes should not be partially rolled out with mixed tracing models.
